# nRF54LM20-DK firmware v0.6.0

Channel Sounding over native USB. **Use native USB** for ranging captures; the
J-Link VCOM transport remains available as the compatibility path, and both
ship in the same archive.

## Highlights

- The initiator's COBS ranging stream and both roles' consoles move from the
  onboard debugger's virtual COM ports to the nRF54LM20 USB 2.0 High-Speed
  device controller (USBHS).
- One native USB cable per DK carries data, console, and power. The onboard
  debugger is needed only for SWD programming and debugging, so it can be
  disconnected during a soak.
- The host still sees ordinary serial ports and the COBS wire format is
  unchanged — no host driver, decoder, or tooling change is needed.
- The four VCOM presets, their names, and their artifacts are unchanged.

## Supported hardware

- **nRF54LM20-DK** (PCA10184), target `nrf54lm20dk/nrf54lm20a/cpuapp`.
- Built as the **A** variant (`nRF54LM20A`), the NPU-less variant for the
  B-silicon DK (`SOC_NRF54LM20A_DEVELOP_IN_NRF54LM20B`). The firmware does not
  use the NPU, so the A target runs on both silicon flavors.
- One 2.4 GHz trace antenna and one RF path; no antenna switch and no RF
  supply rail.
- The bench boards are engineering-sample A silicon (`nRF54LM20A ENGA`).

| Transport | COBS data | Console |
|-----------|-----------|---------|
| Native USB (recommended) | Initiator CDC ACM function `if00` (label `CS Data`) | Initiator `if02`; reflector `if00` (label `Console`) |
| J-Link VCOM (compatibility) | VCOM0 (`uart30`), 1,000,000 baud, 8N1, no flow control | VCOM1 (`uart20`), 115200 baud |

The native USB link negotiates 480 Mbit/s high speed on the DK. A
full-speed-only host falls back to 12 Mbit/s, which works but is parity-only
and does not meet the transport-headroom criterion. CDC ACM ignores the
configured baud rate; open the data port at 1,000,000 baud to match the VCOM
workflow.

## Firmware variants

`cs-ranging-firmware.zip` contains **eight images**: four VCOM and four native
USB.

| File | Role | Mode | Preset | Transport |
|------|------|------|--------|-----------|
| `initiator_nrf54lm20dk_cent_a1_1.hex` | Initiator | RAS | `nrf54lm20dk_cent_a1_1` | J-Link VCOM |
| `reflector_nrf54lm20dk_peri_a1_1.hex` | Reflector | RAS | `nrf54lm20dk_peri_a1_1` | J-Link VCOM |
| `initiator_nrf54lm20dk_cent_a1_1_ipt.hex` | Initiator | IPT | `nrf54lm20dk_cent_a1_1_ipt` | J-Link VCOM |
| `reflector_nrf54lm20dk_peri_a1_1_ipt.hex` | Reflector | IPT | `nrf54lm20dk_peri_a1_1_ipt` | J-Link VCOM |
| `initiator_nrf54lm20dk_usb_cent_a1_1.hex` | Initiator | RAS | `nrf54lm20dk_usb_cent_a1_1` | Native USB |
| `reflector_nrf54lm20dk_usb_peri_a1_1.hex` | Reflector | RAS | `nrf54lm20dk_usb_peri_a1_1` | Native USB |
| `initiator_nrf54lm20dk_usb_cent_a1_1_ipt.hex` | Initiator | IPT | `nrf54lm20dk_usb_cent_a1_1_ipt` | Native USB |
| `reflector_nrf54lm20dk_usb_peri_a1_1_ipt.hex` | Reflector | IPT | `nrf54lm20dk_usb_peri_a1_1_ipt` | Native USB |

Flash a **matched** pair: the same ranging mode (RAS **or** IPT). The two
modes use different BLE discovery and do not pair with each other. Flash both
boards on the same transport as well: the transport changes only the host-side
path, so a mixed pair still forms a BLE link, but one host setup would not see
both boards.

## Install

1. Download `cs-ranging-firmware.zip` from this release.
2. Flash one DK with the initiator image and one with the reflector image,
   using the on-board J-Link (`nrfutil device program --firmware <file>.hex`
   or the nRF Connect Programmer app).
3. **Native USB (recommended):** disconnect the J-Link cable and run each DK
   from its native USB port. Identify the ports:
   - **Linux** — `/dev/serial/by-id/usb-Metirionic_Mars_CS_Initiator_<serial>-if00`
     is the data port and `...-if02` the console;
     `/dev/serial/by-id/usb-Metirionic_Mars_CS_Reflector_<serial>-if00` is the
     reflector console. `<serial>` is the SoC-derived USB serial.
   - **Windows 10+** — the initiator shows two `USB Serial Device (COMx)`
     entries under Device Manager → Ports (COM & LPT), the reflector one. Open
     each candidate at 115200: the one that prints readable logs is the
     console; the other initiator port is data. No vendor driver is required.
   - **macOS** — the initiator exposes two `/dev/cu.usbmodem*` nodes, the
     reflector one. Identify the console the same way: the node that prints
     readable logs at 115200.
   - Open the data port at 1,000,000 baud, 8N1, no flow control. It streams as
     soon as the host configures the device; there is no DTR handshake.
4. **J-Link VCOM (compatibility):** keep the J-Link cable connected. Open the
   initiator's VCOM0 at 1,000,000 baud for the COBS stream and VCOM1 at 115200
   for the console.

The full procedure, including the eight-image selection and per-OS port
identification, is in the
[flash quickstart](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/blob/v0.6.0/docs/flash-quickstart.md).
The transport details and NCS constraints are in the
[hardware reference](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/blob/v0.6.0/docs/hardware.md#native-usb-transport).

## Validation

Bench gate [#20](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/20) ran
the A/B comparison on the physical DK pair on 2026-10-22 (Europe/Berlin):
ten-minute soaks for VCOM and USB in both ranging modes, with the existing
release assertions plus zero backlog drops at the default cadence and a
480 Mbit/s link on every USB run.

| Run | Serialization runs | Valid frames | Event frames | Invalid | Empty proc. | Reflector aborts | Watchdog (init/refl) | Backlog (serialize/diag) | USB drops | Wire rate | Result |
|-----|-------------------:|-------------:|-------------:|--------:|------------:|-----------------:|----------------------|---------------------------|----------:|-----------|--------|
| VCOM RAS | 1846 | 5537 | 3691 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | — | 0.656 Mbit/s | PASS |
| VCOM IPT | 1847 | 5537 | 3691 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | — | 0.656 Mbit/s | PASS |
| USB RAS | 1837 | 5519 | 3679 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 | 0.654 Mbit/s | PASS |
| USB IPT | 1843 | 5528 | 3685 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0 | 0.655 Mbit/s | PASS |

The interval-1 headroom run (USB RAS, 600 s) applied the controller's clamped
`procedure interval: 2` and measured **406,290 B/s = 3.250 Mbit/s** (0.68 % of
the 480 Mbit/s link) with **zero USB transport drops**, zero serialize and
diagnostic backlog drops, zero reflector aborts, and zero watchdog recoveries
(27,478 valid frames, 18,284 event, 0 invalid). The 21 empty-procedure
signatures (0.23 %) are the CS scheduler at the clamped cadence, not a
transport limit; at the same cadence on VCOM the old path saw thousands of
handoff drops. The 480 Mbit/s link rate is not a throughput promise: the
measured bring-up baseline for the USB stack is 2.34 MB/s.

Fault injection passed:

- **Boot with no host** (120 s, data port attached at 30 s): the firmware
  stayed alive, logged one expected pre-attach drop, then streamed 839 valid
  frames with zero post-attach drops.
- **Host stall** (60 s, reader stopped at 20 s): a drop was logged about 1.2 s
  after the boundary, the firmware stayed alive, and reopening the port
  resumed streaming.
- **Literal close/reopen**: one drop was logged after the close, and streaming
  resumed on reopen with no watchdog recovery.

Gate provenance: harness at
[`89f069f`](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/commit/89f069f)
(self-test 206/206); firmware source identical to v0.4.0
([`854fa0a`](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/commit/854fa0a)).
Benches: initiator J-Link `1051890544` / USB serial `9C78D7185741F728`,
reflector J-Link `1051808351` / USB serial `F71FC00462052101`. Each USB run
started from a verified fresh boot so the drop counter began at zero.

## Known issues and constraints

- **High speed is experimental in NCS v3.4.0.** Nordic describes high-speed
  support that way; the bench measured a working 480 Mbit/s link on the DK.
- **Full speed is parity-only.** The 12 Mbit/s fallback carries the same data
  and console but does not meet the transport-headroom criterion.
- **NCSDK-38624.** CDC ACM serial initialization at boot can hang an
  nRF54LM20 until the USB cable is disconnected. USB builds disable that path
  (`CONFIG_CDC_ACM_SERIAL_INITIALIZE_AT_BOOT=n`) and enable the UDC on VBUS
  attach instead. This is an avoidance, not an SDK fix.
- **DRGN-29129.** USB high speed shares HFCLK24M with MPSL; USB is initialized
  after the BLE stack to keep the MPSL ordering safe.
- **DRGN-29277 is deferred.** The sleep-current workaround after USB
  disconnect is not in this release. HFCLK24M remains active while USB is in
  use, so sleep-current targets need the follow-up power-management work.
- **VBUS removal is designed but not bench-tested.** The UDC disables on the
  VBUS-removed message without a reboot, but the gate exercised boot with no
  host and a host stall/close, not a literal port-power removal.
- **The console is best-effort.** Its 1 KiB TX ring and the bounded deferred
  log queue can delay or drop messages, especially before enumeration. Open
  the data port before or at boot to capture the first procedures.
- **The USB identity uses development IDs.** VID `0x1915` and PIDs `0x0001` /
  `0x0002` are Nordic development values; a USB-IF VID/PID remains pre-product
  work.
- **Windows and macOS coverage is manual.** Linux is the merge and release
  gate; the other hosts are release smoke tests
  ([#24](https://github.com/Metirionic/mars-cs-nrf54lm/issues/24)).
- **Programming and recovery stay on SWD.** There is no USB bootloader or DFU
  interface and MCUboot is not used; USB host mode is not available.
- **Do not open the VCOM data port at 921600.** The DK's J-Link bridge
  supports up to 1 Mbps and explicitly does not support 921600; the firmware
  uses 1,000,000 baud.
- **Secure application-core only.** TF-M and non-secure-image USB ownership
  are unverified; the supported builds are the `.../cpuapp` targets.

## Compatibility

- The COBS wire format and the `mars-bluetooth-hci` API are unchanged; the
  same host decoder works over both transports.
- The four VCOM presets keep their names, composition, and artifacts.
- Both transports ship in one archive. Use VCOM for hosts without native USB,
  for a J-Link-only setup, or as the A/B comparison basis.
